name: Vesper-Deep
description: Vesper-Deep is a dense iron-hearted rock orbiting just outside the system's asteroid belt, scarred by constant infall from its crowded neighborhood. Tectonic rift valleys split the southern hemisphere in glowing seams where residual heat still escapes, and compasses anywhere on the surface spin slowly, tracking magnetic anomalies that migrate like herds. The sky is black and hard, thick with drifting belt debris.

With no atmosphere there is only silence and contrast: sunside rock hot enough to blister glove palms, shadow cold enough to crack them, twilight zones forever poised between. The rift valleys exhale faint metallic vapor that freezes into glittering hoarfrost along their rims—the closest thing this world has to weather.

The Halvorsen Mining Consortium worked the titanium lodes of the great northern rift for eleven years, then went bankrupt overnight; their processing towers still stand lit by emergency power nobody admits to paying for. Three hundred kilometers away, a field of escape pod wreckage tells the rest of the story badly: forty pods launched, none reached any known rescue ship, and the pods' logs end with coordinates pointing back at the mining complex.

The uranium and titanium remain the richest untapped claims in the sector, and the bankruptcy court auction is next quarter. But survey drones keep losing signal over the pod field, and the last two crews hired to strip the complex resigned within days of arrival—both citing the same detail: someone inside has been turning the lights on.
